messages:
alice (AcmeCorp): Hey team — we're seeing weird behavior from the embeddings endpoint. Some requests that used to return 1536-dim vectors are returning 768-dim, and cache hit rates look... inconsistent. Started yesterday after we scaled batch size.

maya (Support): Sorry to hear that — can you paste a repro curl or SDK snippet and an example of the two different responses? Also which model/version you pinned?

alice (AcmeCorp): Pinned to 'open-embed-1536:v2'. Minimal repro:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XXX" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"open-embed-1536:v2","inputs":["hello","world"],"batch_size":8}'
```
Response sometimes:
- correct: vectors length 1536
- bad: vectors length 768
We also see cache-miss spikes in our logs, even for repeated inputs.

chris (Eng): Very helpful. Two separate problems could look similar: model selection fallback (e.g., runtime falling back to a quantized 768 variant) OR cache key collisions where prefixing is wrong and returns a different model's cached vector. Can you share the exact headers you send (esp any custom X- headers) and whether you use our SDK which sets `cache_prefix`?

alice (AcmeCorp): We set a custom header for routing from our side: `X-Customer-Tag: acme-prod`. No X-Cache-Prefix. We do use SDK (python) but sometimes call raw curl for smoke tests.

sam (ML Infra): FYI embed-bot shows some cache events around that timeframe. Pasting lines from redis-access logs (sanitized):
```
[2026-04-12T15:03:21Z] cache_lookup key=prefix:abcd1234:open-embed-1536:v2:sha1(....) -> MISS
[2026-04-12T15:03:21Z] cache_store key=prefix:abcd1234:open-embed-768:q8:v1:sha1(....) size=3072
[2026-04-12T15:03:22Z] cache_lookup key=prefix:abcd1234:open-embed-1536:v2:sha1(....) -> HIT
```
Notice the keys sometimes show `open-embed-768` even though request asked for 1536. That suggests routing fallback or a bug where `model` field is truncated or overwritten when we compute prefix for storage.

embed-bot: Observability: request_id=ctx-8f2e, route=emb-prod-eu, model_requested=open-embed-1536:v2, model_used=open-embed-768:q8:v1, cache_hit=false, latency=142ms.

maya (Support): That matches the customer's report. Are those redis keys shared across tenants? Could be prefix reuse if tenant id is not included in keyspace.

sam (ML Infra): Good catch. Current prefix composition is: `prefix:{short_tag}:{model_base}:{shard}` where `short_tag` was supposed to be tenant-derived. There's an old optimization where we truncate tenant tag to 8 chars to reduce key length. Hypothesis: two different tenants with similar short_tag collide after truncation, or truncation + routing hash sometimes pick wrong model_base when batch metadata is large and we hit a codepath that uses `batch_signature[:8]` instead of `tenant_tag[:8]`.

chris (Eng): Another factor: we added an experimental batching optimization last week that deduplicates by `payload_signature` and then reuses a cached embedding from the dedupe map. If dedupe map key uses truncated prefix, it can accidentally match across model variants. That would explain 768 vs 1536 differences.

alice (AcmeCorp): Is there any chance of data leakage between customers? We're concerned if we get someone else's embeddings.

sam (ML Infra): Short answer: unlikely that we return someone else's tenant data because cache entries are scoped, but this bug could cause wrong model variant to be returned for the same tenant. We're investigating whether tenant_id is reliably included. We're also checking if the dedupe map keys included `model_size` in the signature.

maya (Support): We're opening an escalation with Eng. For triage: please confirm
- a full curl request (headers + body) that reproduces the 768 result reliably
- server-side request_id(s) if present
- any timing (approx times you saw bad resp)

alice (AcmeCorp): I can reproduce on demand, here's two request ids from our smoke: `ctx-8f2e` (bad), `ctx-8f4b` (good), timestamps yesterday 15:03:21Z and 15:04:10Z. I'll keep them open.

chris (Eng): Thanks. I ran a quick local sim and found a repro that flips when batch_size >= 8 and when the SDK attaches `X-Customer-Tag` longer than 12 chars. Code snippet we used to repro:
```python
from redwood import EmbeddingsClient
client = EmbeddingsClient(api_key="sk-test-xxx")
client._set_header("X-Customer-Tag","acme-production-1")
client.embeddings(model="open-embed-1536:v2", inputs=["hello"]*8, batch_size=8)
```
Result: 50% of calls returned 768-dim.

sam (ML Infra): Root cause confirmed in local: when building the dedupe key we construct `k = f"{tenant_tag[:8]}:{model_name}:{sig[:12]}"`. But tenant_tag came from header parsing which for long tags included dash characters; we normalize later but forgot to normalize before truncation, resulting in collisions with other tags after truncation. Also `model_name` may be rewritten to the quantized variant in a follow-up step and we were using the pre-rewrite value in the key for lookup but the post-rewrite value for storage. Two separate bugs.

chris (Eng): Plan: immediate hotfix to ensure tenant_tag uses full stable tenant_id (not truncation) in cache/dedupe keys, and ensure we compute model_name canonicalization before generating keys. We'll ship a canary to 5% of requests in the next deploy.

bill (Billing): Related FYI — we've been getting flagged about surprising billing for embeddings: cache_miss counts were up which increases billable tokens. If this is a regression from last week's deploy, we should notify customers who saw spike and offer credits. Can support pull usage delta for AcmeCorp?

maya (Support): Will run usage delta and share. Alice, we'll keep you updated and issue a credit if your calls were affected.

alice (AcmeCorp): Appreciate that. Any workaround while you patch?

sam (ML Infra): Short-term workaround: explicitly set `X-Cache-Prefix` header to a stable value derived from your tenant id and model (e.g., `tenant:acme-id:open-embed-1536:v2`). Example curl: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XXX" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "X-Cache-Prefix: tenant:acme-id:open-embed-1536:v2" \n  -d '{"model":"open-embed-1536:v2","inputs":["hello","world"],"batch_size":8}'
```
This forces the server to use your explicit prefix generation and avoids the buggy truncation path. Not ideal long term but should prevent cross-variant matches.

chris (Eng): Also a safe short-term mitigation on our side: disable the experimental dedupe map for batching for all affected routes until the canary proves green. Doing that now.

embed-bot: Deploy started: canary=5%, change_id=chg-20260412-09, diff=ensure model canonicalization before key generation, disable dedupe map toggle.

maya (Support): Alice — I'll DM you a minimal wrapper to set X-Cache-Prefix automatically if you want. We'll also log the affected request ids for postmortem.

alice (AcmeCorp): Thanks. Patch looks good. We'll try the workaround and watch hit rates. Please add me to updates.

chris (Eng): After canary completes we'll roll. ETA 2 hours. We'll follow up with details in this thread and a short postmortem with root cause, timeline, and credits.

sam (ML Infra): Postmortem note: root cause = two bugs: (1) truncation/normalization order for tenant tags leading to collisions in dedupe/cache keys, (2) key generation order used pre-rewrite model name for lookup and post-rewrite name for storage. Both combined produced wrong-dimension vectors being returned.

bill (Billing): I'll prepare a billing impact estimate for AcmeCorp against the spike window.

alice (AcmeCorp): Confirmed workaround fixed it for smoke tests, hit-rate back to expected, no more 768 responses. Thanks for fast action :thumbsup:

maya (Support): Great — closing escalation when we have canary + one hour stable. Will file the follow-up PM notes. :white_check_mark:
